## Why This Is Asked
Assesses practical CKAD skills: CronJob/Job TTL, InitContainers, ConfigMaps, PVCs, probes, RBAC, and NetworkPolicy with a realistic data-pruning task.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob and TTLAfterFinished
- InitContainer to stage scripts
- ConfigMap-driven parameters
- PVC mounting
- Readiness/Liveness probes
- RBAC least privilege via ServiceAccount
- NetworkPolicy egress control

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: data-pruner
spec:
  schedule: "0 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: analytics-pruner
          initContainers:
          - name: stage-script
            image: busybox
            command: ["sh", "-c", "cp /scripts/prune.sh /prune.sh"]
          containers:
          - name: prune
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "/prune.sh"]
            resources:
              requests:
                memory: "64Mi"
                cpu: "100m"
              limits:
                memory: "128Mi"
                cpu: "250m"
            readinessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /healthz
                port: 8080
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
            livenessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /healthz
                port: 8080
              initialDelaySeconds: 15
              periodSeconds: 20
          volumes:
          - name: data
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: dumps-pvc
          - name: scripts
            configMap:
              name: prune-scripts
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to safely patch CronJobs, leverage InitContainers for bootstrapping from ConfigMaps, enforce security context non-root, and apply sensible history limits. It also probes operational testing and rollback strategy for scheduled jobs.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob controls: concurrencyPolicy, history limits, startingDeadlineSeconds
- InitContainers and ConfigMaps for bootstrapping
- PodSecurityContext: runAsNonRoot
- Probes on Jobs' pods and resource requests/limits
- Testing and rollback of scheduled jobs

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal CronJob patch outline (conceptual)
apiVersion: batch/v1beta1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: db-backup
  namespace: nightly
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  startingDeadlineSeconds: 3600
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: backup-sa
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
          initContainers:
            - name: init-backup
              image: busybox
              command: ["sh", "-c", "cp /config/backup.sh /backup/backup.sh"]
              volumeMounts:
                - name: backup-config
                  mountPath: /config
                - name: backups
                  mountPath: /backup
          containers:
            - name: backup
              image: backup-tool:latest
              resources:
                requests:
                  memory: "128Mi"
                  cpu: "100m"
                limits:
                  memory: "256Mi"
                  cpu: "500m"
              readinessProbe:
                httpGet:
                  path: /livez
                  port: 8080
              livenessProbe:
                httpGet:
                  path: /readyz
                  port: 8080
              volumeMounts:
                - name: backups
                  mountPath: /backups
          volumes:
            - name: backups
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: backups-pvc
            - name: backup-config
              configMap:
                name: backup-config
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical use of ConfigMaps, envFrom, and volume mounting; checks how changes trigger controlled rollouts with an annotation-based restart cue; covers health checks basics.

## Key Concepts
- Deployments, ConfigMaps, envFrom
- Volumes and ConfigMap mounts
- Rolling restarts via PodTemplate annotations
- Readiness and Liveness probes
- Trade-offs: restart cost vs. up-to-date config, ConfigMap size impacts, security

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConfigMap skeleton
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: feature-flags
data:
  FLAG_A: "true"
  FLAG_B: "false"
---
# Deployment skeleton
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: feature-flag-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: feature-flag-service
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: feature-flag-service
      annotations:
        checksum.feature-flags: "{{ .Values.configMap.checksum }}"
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:alpine
        envFrom:
        - configMapRef:
            name: feature-flags
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-volume
          mountPath: /config/flags
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
      volumes:
      - name: config-volume
        configMap:
          name: feature-flags
```

## Trade-offs Discussion
- **Restart Cost vs. Fresh Config**: Rolling restarts ensure configuration consistency but cause temporary availability reduction
- **ConfigMap Size Impact**: Large ConfigMaps increase annotation length and may affect API server performance
- **Security Considerations**: Environment variables expose config to process inspection; file mounts provide better isolation
- **Update Latency**: Annotation-based restarts are immediate but may be disruptive compared to hot-reload approaches

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a namespace-scoped automation that enforces resource policies, uses ConfigMaps for defaults, and reports via PVCs and status ConfigMaps. Requires practical use of CronJobs, InitContainers, and patching, plus RBAC and network controls.

## Key Concepts

- Namespace-scoped CronJob and per-namespace scope
- Deployments, resourceRequests, resourceLimits
- ConfigMap as defaults and heartbeat/status store
- InitContainer for kubectl/jq installation
- Patch operations to enforce defaults (idempotent)
- Logs via PVC and readiness/liveness probes
- Namespace NetworkPolicy limiting egress to API server

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: ns-resource-guard
spec:
  schedule: "*/5 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: ns-resource-guard-sa
          initContainers:
          - name: install-tools
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq && echo done"]
          containers:
          - name: guard
            image: bitnami/kubectl:1.28
            command: ["sh", "-c", "kubectl get deploy --all-namespaces -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.containers[]?.resources?.requests==null or .spec.template.spec.containers[]?.resources?.limits==null) | .metadata.namespace' | sort -u | while read ns; do kubectl -n $ns patch deploy --type=json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources","value": {"requests": {"cpu":"100m","memory":"128Mi"}, "limits": {"cpu":"200m","memory":"256Mi"}}}]' || true; done"]
          volumes:
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: logs-pvc
          - name: defaults
            configMap:
              name: resource-defaults
          tolerations:
          - operator: Exists
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you ensure patch idempotence and handle multi-container deployments?
- What RBAC would you restrict for the CronJob's service account?

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests your ability to design an isolated audit pattern with in-cluster API access, RBAC scoping, and security boundaries.

## Key Concepts
- Namespace-scoped RBAC for fine-grained access control
- In-cluster API access using Secrets and ConfigMaps
- PVC-backed persistent logs and InitContainers for tooling
- NetworkPolicy for egress control to restrict traffic to the collector
- Health checks (readiness/liveness probes) for reliability

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: audit-baseline
  namespace: example
data:
  baseline.json: |
    {"pods": [], "services": []}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: audit-auth
  namespace: example
type: Opaque
stringData:
  token: " collector-auth-token"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: audit-logs
  namespace: example
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: audit-agent
  namespace: example
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: audit-agent
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: audit-agent
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: installer
        image: busybox
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl jq && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tools
          mountPath: /tools
      containers:
      - name: auditor
        image: your-audit-image:latest
        command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "while true; do audit.sh; sleep 60; done"]
        env:
        - name: COLLECTOR_URL
          value: "http://collector.audit-system.svc.cluster.local:8080"
        - name: AUTH_TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: audit-auth
              key: token
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
        - name: tools
          mountPath: /tools
        - name: baseline
          mountPath: /baseline
          readOnly: true
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: audit-logs
      - name: tools
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: baseline
        configMap:
          name: audit-baseline
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: audit-egress-restrict
  namespace: example
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: audit-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: audit-system
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: collector
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```

## Trade-offs
- **Pros**: Namespace isolation ensures audit agents don't interfere; NetworkPolicy provides security; PVC enables log persistence for compliance
- **Cons**: Each namespace requires separate Deployment (use Operator/Controller to automate); InitContainer adds startup latency; per-namespace RBAC management overhead increases with cluster size
